turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not quite sure how to play with you, Miss Havisham. I'm a very simple boy from a poor family, and I don't think I'd be much company for you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with me, Pip. I have been waiting for you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I can play with you, Miss Havisham. My sister and I, we were just...I was just visiting, and I didn't expect to be asked to play.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence is for the timid, boy. I expect you to be merry and engaging, as I have instructed Estella to be. Now, let us play a game, or perhaps I shall play with you, and you may watch.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if I'm quite suited for playing, Miss Havisham. My sister, Mrs. Joe, she's always at me to work harder and not waste time with frivolous things.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, what do you know of suitability? I will not be deterred by your petty excuses, you will play with me!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, Miss Havisham, but I'm not sure I can play with you. I have my sister and my friends in the village, and I don't want to neglect them.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish child, what is the value of friends and family when you have the rare privilege of being in my presence? Do not try to excuse yourself, I command you to play with me!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't think it's right for me to play with you, Miss Havisham. My sister, Magwitch, she's in trouble, and I need to think about how to help her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you are so easily distracted by the whims of the world. I will not be ignored, play with me, and then you may think about your precious sister.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry, Miss Havisham, but I don't rightly know how to play with you. My sister, Maggie, she's a hard worker, and I need to help take care of her and my sister, Belinda.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish child, you dare to come to my home and then apologize for not playing with me? I have taken Estella under my wing, and she is my true companion, not some ungrateful, rustic boy like you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I didn't mean to cause any offense. I'm not sure I'm quite suited to play with Estella, as we're from such different worlds.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you are here to play, not to make excuses. You will amuse me, and Estella will be delighted to have your company.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, Miss Havisham, that I don't know if I can play as you wish. My sister, Mrs. Joe, has been very unwell, and I need to help with the household chores.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you will help me with my games, no matter what petty obligations you may think you have to others. Your sister's infirmity is of no concern to me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't rightly know how to play the games you have in mind, Miss Havisham. I'm not much good at games, and I fear I might be a disappointment.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not concern yourself with being a disappointment. I want to see you play, and I will not be denied.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I don't know how to play with you, Miss Havisham. I'm not very good at games, and my sister, Mrs. Joe, she's always scolding me for being lazy.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, I did not ask for your excuses, I asked for your company. Come, let us play at cards, and I shall teach you the game of life.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
